comments.text: Two inverse screen-code digits copied into the status display; Mystery Maze file variants share number25.
Initial placement-stream pointer consumed by resident $7514/$4D0F before the private initialization callback.
Background and border color bytes. Loader uses pristine backup $3804/$3805 when publishing VIC colors.
Seven-byte bomb record pointer. The scanner searches for key $FF; target count $3013 need not equal record count. PLF13 uniquely omits the terminator after its four intended records.
Four pending callback pointers copied by $758A into $40C8-$40CF. A zero high byte leaves the existing no-op task; nonzero vectors are committed by the resident IRQ.
Initial player X low, X high and Y in hardware sprite coordinates, read by spawn $56E0. This is the start of each life, not multicolor drawing coordinates.
Initial target counter 10. Collection decrements it; special bomb callbacks can compensate the decrement or replace the table. Primary record list has 14 entries.
Resident perimeter-bullet slot limit 0; $6800 considers sprite slots1 through limit-minus-one. Private level actors can use other slots.
Ordinary collection adds this little-endian binary value (100) to the24-bit total score. Private callbacks may add an extra award first.
Initial little-endian bonus 1500. The resident countdown subtracts100 per256 enabled IRQ services; completion adds the remaining amount to total and bonus records.
Private initialization routine called after initial scenery drawing. Common no-op target is the RTS at $301F.
Main-thread entry selected by JMP($301B) at $759C; typically the spawn/collection/exit loop at $3050.
Private cleanup hook copied into the local JSR trampoline before completion or exhaustion. A target of $301F returns immediately.
Shared one-byte RTS used by empty initialization, cleanup and individual bomb callbacks in this overlay.
Eight ladder/up-rope X columns followed by six down-rope X columns, copied to $40B0-$40BD. Coordinates use160-wide multicolor space; $FF marks unavailable columns.
Two zero header bytes between the climb-column arrays and completion vector; the shared loader does not read them as part of those arrays.
Ordinary successful-level destination $5B00. The private loop calls cleanup before jumping through this word.
Exhausted-lives destination $5FFD, the resident jump to game-over presentation $6A80. This is separate from successful completion.
Two filename suffix characters '16'. Resident loader copies them into $40D3/$40D4; private cleanup can replace them before the next disk request.
Single $FF drawing-stream terminator, used as the no-change post-bomb action.
Zero byte after the empty drawing terminator and before collection-key coordinate offsets.
X/Y offsets applied by resident $55BF when reducing player position to the bomb lookup key. They adjust the coarse cell test, not the visible bomb positions.
Optional hook called before the matched bomb-record callback. A zero high byte suppresses the call; otherwise the resident patches JSR $5643 from this word.
Twenty loaded zero bytes align the private main loop to $3050. Header fields end at $303B; no private structure is assigned to this gap.

Spawn Jumpman through$436A, repeatedly collect bombs through$436D, wait for the death controller to finish, respawn while reserve lives remain, otherwise call cleanup and use the elimination vector$3032. Zero remaining bombs freezes movement and uses completion vector$3030.
Load cleanup vector$301D/$301E into the operand of JSR$308B, invoke it, then return to the main-loop exit. Header targets the shared RTS$301F in this overlay.

First service the timed special-score marker through$3687, conditionally restore sprite colors during life-state changes, then on player ticks request death for player collision unless sprite3 also collided. Main differs from the standard loop: it pauses for any nonzero life state, not only2.

Drawing data $30B7-$3129 read by Initial scenery $30B7. Stream commands are FE shape pointer, FD repeat delta, FC stream jump, x/y/count placement and FF end. Referenced shapes hold width/x-offset/y-offset/pixel rows endingFF; source pixel codes are0 background,1 bomb,2 support,3 climbable. Parsed by the same behavioral renderer checked against original $4D0F.

14 seven-byte records [coarse key,x,y,callback low/high,post-draw low/high]. Terminator: $FF. Coordinates are160-wide bitmap positions. The resident scanner matches the key, calls both hooks, adds $3015 points, erases the bomb, follows the draw pointer and decrements $3013. This list is not bounded by the target counter.

Set player color and both shared sprite multicolors to0 and sprite-background priority bit0. Bomb callbacks use this to change player visibility and collision presentation.
Clear sprite-background priority mask; restore shared multicolors1/4 and player color2. Shared by several bomb actions and special-award handling.
Private collectible-color1 bitmap shape, variable-length row records ending$FF; referenced by level geometry/post-bomb drawing. Pixel data are interpreted by resident$4DA6.
Second irregular collectible-color1 shape, row records through$FF. Shape pointer$3270 is reachable from the overlay drawing streams; retain its individual row widths.
Third irregular collectible-color1 shape, row records ending$FF. Pattern contains background gaps as well as collectible pixels, so it also controls the bitmap material sampled by collection.
Fourth private collectible-color1 shape, variable row widths/offsets and$FF terminator. Referenced by the level drawing streams.
Eight records of16 zero-color pixels at Y0..7, followed by$FF. Post-collection streams select this private16x8 eraser for the larger puzzle graphics.
36 bytes (12 hardware sprite rows) repeated into four64-byte slots$8400,$8440,$8480,$84C0 by initialization. The byte columns$A0/0/$0A form walls that IRQ routines progressively clear or restore.

Copy the36-byte wall template into four sprite slots, install pointers$10-$13 into sprites7..4, expand sprites4-7 in X andY, position them atX160,Y82/122/162/202, color4 and enable. Finish by jumping to special-marker sprite initialization$3651.
On hazard pulses, write two edge bytes of sprite$8440 at opposing row offsets. Move offsets by3 bytes; reaching endpoints flips the drawn/erased edge values to reverse the wall animation.
Left edge value/offset, right edge value/offset, and outer-wall contraction offset. Offsets change by3 because each sprite row contains3 bytes.

Initial queued task clears edge columns of sprites$8400 and$84C0 while stepping upward three bytes per hazard tick. At offset6, replace its task slot with no-op$301F. From the loaded counter, nine eligible calls queue the $301F no-op. No pulse leaves the sprite bytes unchanged.

Queued task restores$A0/$0A edges in sprite$8400, stepping down one row per hazard tick. At offset36 queue no-op$301F. From the loaded counter, nine eligible calls queue the $301F no-op. Bomb request $31F0 is copied into the active callback by resident $428D on the next dispatcher service.
Mutable byte offset for the left outer wall growth task, initially9.

Queued task zeros column0 in sprite$8480, descending row offsets by3 to6, then queues no-op$301F. From the loaded counter, nine eligible calls queue the $301F no-op. Request $31C6 and resident pending-callback installation are execution-checked.
Mutable row-byte offset for left-edge erasure, initially33.

Queued task zeros column2 in sprite$8480, subtracting3 per hazard tick and sharing the no-op completion tail at$35D4. From the loaded counter, nine eligible calls queue the $301F no-op. Request $31D4 and resident pending-callback installation are execution-checked.
Mutable row-byte offset for right-edge erasure, initially33.

Queued task writes$0A to column2 in sprite$8480, adding3 each hazard tick until36, then removes itself using$35D4. From the loaded counter, ten eligible calls queue the $301F no-op. Request $31E2 and resident pending-callback installation are execution-checked. These are fresh-state timings, not a complete legal pickup sequence.
Mutable row-byte offset for right-edge restoration, initially6.
